_comment: Component-body overlaps that are accepted, for ACCEPTANCE H (scripts/64_body_overlap.py). A pair listed here is still reported; it just does not fail the gate. Add an entry only for a mechanical decision someone has actually taken, and write down who took it and why.

allow.why: The regulator body overhangs the M2 mounting hole H4 after the L1 repair moved it clear of the hole's copper. H4 is a bare drilled hole, not a part: nothing is placed there, so nothing collides at assembly. What it constrains is the enclosure -- the screw head and washer have to clear the SOT-223 body -- which is a mechanical decision taken outside this pipeline.

PEG1 is one of the two NPTH locating pegs of J1 itself. The USB-C receptacle's own body drawing contains them -- that is what they are for -- so the connector's outline is bound to contain them. They are holes, not parts: nothing is placed there and nothing collides at assembly. They exist as separate footprints only because EasyEDA put the drill on the board rather than in the connector, and 13_fix_import.py had to synthesise them as NPTH footprints (S4a) to get them into the drill file at all. 64_body_overlap.py already distinguishes them in the report as part-on-hole rather than part-on-part; this entry stops that distinction being an ACCEPTANCE H failure.
The second of J1's own NPTH locating pegs. Same reasoning as J1/PEG1 above.
